ixiptla.title: What is Ixiptla?
ixiptla.description: Rooted in Nahuatl wisdom, Ixiptla embodies the profound concept of sacred representation. More than mere replication, it captures the essence of transformation - where an object or being becomes a vessel of divine presence, bridging the physical and spiritual realms.
ixiptla.description2: In this exhibition, we explore these sacred vessels through a curated collection of replicas. Each piece tells a story of our ancestral heritage, offering a window into the deep cultural significance of Mesoamerican artistry.

digitalArchaeology.title: Digital Archaeology
digitalArchaeology.description: We explore Mesoamerican cultural heritage through cutting-edge technology, creating immersive experiences that connect past and present.
digitalArchaeology.description2: Each archaeological piece tells a unique story that we preserve digitally for future generations.

mayaCollection.title: Maya Collection
mayaCollection.description: Discover extraordinary artifacts from Maya civilization, from ceremonial vessels to anthropomorphic figures that reveal the complexity of their worldview.
mayaCollection.description2: Each object is a window to the past, meticulously documented and presented in high resolution for study and contemplation.

experience3d.title: 3D Experience
experience3d.description: Immerse yourself in a unique three-dimensional experience where you can interact with artifacts from every angle, appreciating details beyond traditional photography.
experience3d.description2: Modern web technology allows us to create virtual museums accessible from any device.

collection.title: Archaeological Replicas Collection - Ixiptla Museum
collection.description: Explore our curated collection of Mesoamerican archaeological replicas: Maya vessels, Mexica sculptures, Teotihuacan figurines and more historical pieces.
collection.pageDescription: Complete catalog of archaeological replicas from pre-Columbian Mexican cultures. Each piece includes historical information, crafting techniques and cultural context.
